seoTitle: Plus Code Converter: Encode, Decode, Recover Short Codes
metaDescription: Turn latitude and longitude into a Plus Code (Open Location Code), decode one into its area, or expand a short code from a reference. Offline.
intro: Encodes and decodes Open Location Codes, including the 11 to 15 digit refinements, and recovers short codes near a reference point.
why:
Plus Codes give any place a short address without street names. The tool follows the published specification: a 20 character alphabet, five latitude and longitude pairs and an optional grid refinement. Codes were compared with the openlocationcode Python library on 300 random points.

A short code such as 9G8F+6W drops the first characters and is only meaningful near a place. Give a reference location within roughly 50 km to recover the full code. Decoding returns the centre and the corners of the cell, with its size in metres.
howTo: Paste a Plus Code to decode it, or a latitude and longitude to encode.
For a short code, enter a nearby reference as lat, lon.
Pick the code length for encoding; 10 is about 14 by 14 m.

faq.a: 10 digits is the usual precision, about 14 metres; each added digit narrows it further.
Padding in short-area codes such as 8FVC0000+.
No. Plus Codes are an open standard with no database or licence.

faq.q: Can it find a place by name?
faq.a: No. That needs a geocoding service; this tool only converts coordinates.
